A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRMBench study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original PRM and critic-model evaluations, human performance, and experiments examining inference bias, prompting and Best-of-8 selection.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations on physics, chemistry and biology in Appendix B.5.

M1.justification: The data perturbation/filtering pipeline and model-scoring procedure are retained. STEM uses a similar curation methodology; Appendix F presents training ideas as future directions without reporting an implemented or evaluated method change.

E1.justification: v4 adds PRMBench-STEM for fine-grained step-error evaluation in physics, chemistry and biology, containing 1,619, 1,543 and 2,342 instances respectively (Appendix B.5, Table 9). This substantially broadens coverage beyond the original mathematics-centered benchmark while retaining earlier evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding original PRMBench, bias, prompting and BoN experiments. The new STEM tables reuse subsets of previously evaluated PRMs and critic models; they introduce no new comparison method.

E3.justification: The added STEM evaluations introduce separate domain sample sizes and report eight subcategories, without Multi-Solution Consistency (Tables 9–12). Original prompting, human-evaluation sampling, costly-model subsets and Best-of-8 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The inference-bias, error-position, few-shot, BoN-correlation and case-study analyses are retained. The STEM addition supplies domain benchmark scores without introducing a separate ablation, perturbation study or diagnostic protocol.

E5.justification: No run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance procedures are newly introduced. Existing standard-deviation and Somers' D summaries are retained, and the STEM tables report point scores.

E6.justification: Original PRMBench and BoN numerical results are retained, while Tables 10–12 add extensive STEM results. For example, Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B scores 73.7 on biology, 71.4 on chemistry and 71.1 on physics. These substantially extend the empirical record under new conditions, rather than demonstrate same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The category definitions, PRMScore equation, solution-level similarity formula and appendix mathematical examples and counterexamples are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims about the 6,216-instance, 83,456-label benchmark, evaluation of 25 models and weaknesses of existing PRMs. The STEM extension does not redefine those core claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix F discusses reducing Neutral-labeled training samples, contrastive/preference training with error-type labels, and implications for step-level LLM evaluation. Section 8 also explicitly identifies textual reasoning as the current scope and multimodal evaluation as future work.

D1.justification: Existing scoring instructions, prompts, annotator guidance and project/toolkit access information are retained. Appendix B.5 refers to similar curation but provides no new concrete implementation, preprocessing or access instructions.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Qu et al. (2025) on efficient reasoning, Su et al. (2025) on OpenThinkIMG, and Peng Xia et al. (2024a) on MMed-RAG. These are limited contextual additions; existing PRM and benchmark positioning remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds Appendix B.5, Appendix F, acknowledgements and a limitation paragraph, alongside brief main-text pointers, typo corrections and affiliation renumbering. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds a STEM statistics table and three domain-result tables (Tables 9–12), and places the retained BoN tables side by side as Tables 13–14. Existing figures and table designs remain intact, with localized reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The STEM evaluations provide useful evidence about fine-grained error detection across additional scientific domains, and the new discussion clarifies applicability and future research directions. The gain is limited by sparse STEM-specific sourcing and validation details. Appendix B.5's broad weaker-performance summary also needs qualification because results vary by model and category coverage differs from the original benchmark.
